## Plan: Auth link removal and baseline-backed sync recovery

Remove the visible Auth tab entry while preserving the Auth module as a navigable destination from the auth_status widget, add a pending-change indicator to the Sync nav entry, fix incorrect sync change classification, and extend the sync stack to support reverting pending local inserts, updates, and deletes. The recommended approach is to keep the existing page_navbar and main tab routing intact, hide only the Auth tab label, centralize pending-change counting and change typing in sync logic, and base recovery on a project-level baseline snapshot architecture that can later power client-facing backup and restore workflows.

**Steps**
1. Phase 1: Navbar/auth entry cleanup. Update the top-level navigation in /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/ui.R so the Auth destination still exists with value Auth but no redundant visible navbar link. Reuse the existing auth_status click flow from mod_auth_status_server and the parent nav_select observer in /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/server.R. If bslib has no clean hidden-tab primitive in this app, apply a targeted label-hiding approach that preserves tab selection by value and does not disturb other main_tabs navigation.
2. Phase 2: Sync nav pending-count badge. Add a small reactive indicator on the Sync nav label in /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/ui.R and /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/server.R, following the existing dynamic nav item pattern used by output$nav_plot_context. The count source should be a single backend helper in /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/R/logic_sync.R that totals all pending local changes across tracked tables so the nav badge and Sync module use the same source of truth.
3. Phase 3: Correct change typing. Refactor /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/R/logic_sync.R so summary counts and detail cards use the same change classification rules. Replace the current via_env hardcoded update behavior in sync_get_local_changes with shared helper logic that determines insert versus update by checking local rowVersion where available and master.core row existence where needed. This phase also covers the reported site-unit tree case so a newly created SU assignment is counted consistently as insert or update across the accordion badges and detail cards.
4. Phase 4: Introduce project baselines as the recovery foundation. Add baseline snapshot support using the existing project-as-file architecture in /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/R/logic_project.R, especially save_project, open_project, and close_project. The baseline layer should create a restorable project snapshot representing the initial state before local edits, plus metadata describing project_id, creation time, source file path if relevant, and integrity details. This baseline is the primary restore source for later project backup/restore UX and should be reusable outside the Sync module.
5. Phase 5: Define baseline lifecycle and capture points. Decide and implement when a baseline is created or refreshed, using existing project open/create/save flows in /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/R/mod_project.R and project helpers in /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/R/logic_project.R. The preferred rule is to capture a baseline when a project is first opened or attached for editing, and preserve it until the user explicitly accepts/reset/saves a new baseline. This step depends on Phase 4.
6. Phase 6: Add delete tracking to the local sync model. Extend the sync backend in /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/R/logic_sync.R with a durable representation of pending deletes, likely a local tombstone/change-log table keyed by sync table and primary key plus enough payload to reconnect a delete to the baseline-backed restore system. Update local write paths that currently hard-delete rows, especially SU delete/edit flows in /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/R/mod_hierarchy.R and any other push-eligible delete paths, so they record a pending delete instead of discarding revertable state.
7. Phase 7: Revert backend API backed by the baseline model. Add backend functions in /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/R/logic_sync.R to revert one pending change by table and primary key using the baseline architecture as the canonical restore source. Inserts should remove the newly created local row. Updates should restore the row to baseline values, or to the latest clean state if the architecture distinguishes baseline from current clean state. Deletes should recreate the deleted local row from the baseline/tombstone payload and remove the pending delete marker. Validate table names against SYNC_TABLE_CONFIG and return structured success/error messages the UI can display.
8. Phase 8: Sync UI support for revert and auth-gated push. Update /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/R/mod_sync.R to render per-record Revert actions in the diff cards, include delete cards in the change views, and wire button handlers to the new revert backend. Also replace the inline yellow Push changes style with a neutral primary-emphasis treatment from the theme and update enablement logic so the button is disabled and visually greyed out when either there are no pending changes or the user is not authenticated. Add a defensive auth guard in the push observer, not only UI disablement.
9. Phase 9: Ensure local dirty markers and restore metadata are applied consistently. Review and patch write paths that participate in sync but do not currently stamp local_modified_utc or preserve enough information for restore behavior, including /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/R/mod_veg_sample.R save_veg_cell and bulk/create flows in /Users/nicolas/Documents/GitHub/vpro/R/mod_hierarchy.R. This is required so pending counts, badges, revert actions, and push behavior all reflect actual local edits.
10. Phase 10: Verify end-to-end behavior. Smoke-test auth navigation, pending-count rendering, push-button disabling, change classification, revert insert, revert update, revert delete, baseline creation, and the site-unit tree assignment scenario. Confirm that Sync summaries, detail cards, and nav badge counts stay in sync before and after revert/push operations, and that a project-level restore path can be built on the same baseline assets.

**Verification**
1. Launch the app and confirm the top navbar no longer shows a visible Auth label while clicking the auth_status widget still opens the Auth module.
2. Make one pending local insert and one pending local update, then confirm the Sync nav badge increments correctly and matches the total rows shown in the Sync Changes view.
3. Reproduce the site-unit tree reassignment flow from the hierarchy sidebar and verify the Site accordion badge classification matches the detailed change card classification for the same record.
4. Confirm a project baseline is created at the chosen lifecycle point and that its metadata identifies the source project and capture time.
5. While signed out, confirm Push changes is disabled and visually greyed out, and the server-side push handler rejects direct invocation with a sign-in message.
6. While signed in, confirm Push changes uses the new neutral emphasis styling, remains enabled only when pending changes exist, and still routes to Merge Requests on success.
7. Create a pending insert, update, and delete for push-eligible rows and verify each appears in Sync with a working Revert action that restores the local DuckDB state from the baseline-backed model and refreshes counts and cards.
8. Confirm the baseline artifacts are sufficient to support a later full project restore workflow without redesigning the storage model.

**Decisions**
- Included scope: remove only the redundant visible Auth navbar link, not the full top-level navbar.
- Included scope: full delete tracking and delete revert in this block, not just insert/update revert.
- Recommended design: use a project-level baseline snapshot as the main recovery primitive, then layer Sync row-level revert on top of it.
- Recommended reuse: build baselines on top of existing save_project/open_project/close_project mechanics rather than inventing a separate snapshot format first.
- Excluded scope: broader navigation redesign outside the Auth entry, and unrelated sync/push refactors beyond what is required for consistent pending-change and baseline-backed revert behavior.

**Further Considerations**
1. Baseline lifecycle policy still needs one product decision: whether baseline refresh happens automatically after a successful push/save, or only when the user explicitly accepts the current state as the new baseline. My recommendation is explicit acceptance for safety.
2. If per-row revert must work while offline and after many local edits, the baseline design may still need a light local change ledger to identify which fields changed and whether a row was created after baseline capture.
3. The client-facing Backup Current Project menu item in the app can later be implemented as a user-facing wrapper around the same baseline/snapshot infrastructure instead of a separate export path.
